arc: Move ArcSystemStateBridge to chrome/browser/ash/arc/idle_manager

ArcSystemStateBridge is only observed by ArcBackgroundServiceObserver in
chrome/browser/ash/arc/idle_manager/. Move it there as part of removing
the unshipped VMM swap directory, which also eliminates the circular
dependency between idle_manager and vmm.

Bypass-Check-License: Moved files.

[devtools] Make settings a11y web tests independent of tabbedLocation

The DevTools SettingsScreen is being migrated to a declarative
<devtools-tabbed-pane> (https://crrev.com/c/8682801), which removes the
private `tabbedLocation` field. Look up the tabbed pane through the
rendered <devtools-tabbed-pane> element instead, falling back to
`tabbedLocation` until the DevTools change rolls into Chromium.

Revert CHECK to DCHECK in MTPDeviceDelegateImpl::ReadDirectoryInternal

A recent bulk conversion changed a DCHECK(task_in_progress_) to a CHECK
in MTPDeviceDelegateImpl::ReadDirectoryInternal, which caused crashes in
production. This reverts the CHECK back to a DCHECK.

This fix was generated by the Crash Autofix pipeline for crash report
crash/e55d9f2b08400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

cc2be16dc307d39b02667213445dcabd5c48a5f1 [ diff ] 
[Linux] Add BackgroundPortal and use it in BackgroundModeManager

Inside an app sandbox (Flatpak or Snap), running in the background without
open windows and autostarting on login require permission from the
org.freedesktop.portal.Background XDG Desktop Portal.

This CL:
1. Adds a BackgroundPortalClient interface and a default BackgroundPortal
   implementation in //components/dbus/xdg that wrap the portal's
   RequestBackground and SetStatus D-Bus calls. Responses are validated
   strictly: "background" must be present and boolean, and "autostart" must
   be boolean if present. SetStatus messages are made single-line and
   truncated at a valid UTF-8 boundary to fit the portal's length limit.
2. Integrates BackgroundPortalClient into BackgroundModeManager when
   base::nix::GetAppSandbox() reports a sandbox. The portal is asked for
   permission and the matching autostart state when background mode starts,
   when the background clients or the background mode pref change, and when
   a profile is deleted. As for the Windows launch-on-startup registration,
   profile destruction at shutdown doesn't turn off autostart.
3. Avoids prompting users who never need background mode: the first
   RequestBackground call is only made once background mode is entered.
   After that, the portal is kept in sync, e.g. to turn autostart off when
   the last background app is removed. A local state pref,
   background_mode.portal_autostart_granted, records whether the portal
   enabled autostart. If it is set at startup and background mode isn't
   needed any more (e.g. apps were removed while the browser wasn't
   running), the stale autostart entry is turned off once extensions are
   ready. Permission was already granted then, so no dialog is shown.
4. Ignores stale portal responses using a request generation counter.
5. Exits background mode and stops requesting permission for the rest of
   the session once the portal denies it, so extension install/uninstall
   events don't re-prompt.

[protobuf] Add NewPatch for roll_protobuf.py new-patch

Creating a new Chromium local patch in `third_party/protobuf/patches/`
currently requires manually staging `src/` or `python/` edits, writing
a `patches/NNNN-*.patch` diff, amending the commit so its tree and patch
file match, and updating `README.chromium` by hand.

That multi-step manual sequence is error-prone during an active roll and
leaves `state.json` `expected_head` out of sync when a new patch commit
is added on a `replayed` roll branch.

Add `NewPatchResult`, `NewPatch`, and `FormatNewPatchReport` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to turn uncommitted `src/` and
`python/` edits into a numbered `patches/NNNN-*.patch` file and an
`"Apply patches/NNNN-*.patch"` commit in one step, normalize committed
worktree files, and advance `state.json` `expected_head` when on a
`replayed` roll branch.

[protobuf] Add worktree validation and normalization helpers

`roll_protobuf.py` currently serializes refreshed patch files during
`continue` without excluding companion notes under `patches/`, and has
no shared helpers for validating `NNNN-<slug>.patch` names, scoping
uncommitted working-tree edits to `src/` and `python/`, or normalizing
committed worktree line endings.

Without those helpers, the upcoming `new-patch` and `fixup` commands
cannot reject active git operations or out-of-scope edits outside `src/`
and `python/`, and checkouts with `core.autocrlf=true` can leave `.git`
stat-cache mismatches after creating or amending patch commits.

Add `_IsGitOperationInProgress`, `_NormalizeNewPatchName`,
`_IsAllowedLocalPatchPath`, `_CollectUncommittedPatchPaths`,
`_BuildPatchDiffFromCommit`, `_RefreshPatchFileFromHeadCommit`, and
`_NormalizeCommittedWorktreeFiles` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` with unit tests in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf_test.py`.

[protobuf] Cache RollProtobufTest git fixtures in setUpClass

`RollProtobufPlanTest` and `RollProtobufStartTest` currently create and
populate their paired baseline git repositories from scratch inside each
test method's `setUp()`, while `_ResolveCheckoutPaths` and
`LoadRollState` spawn fresh `git rev-parse` subprocesses even when a
caller already resolved `_CheckoutPaths`.

As M6 adds `new-patch` and `fixup` integration tests, rebuilding those
git fixtures per test method and re-running `git rev-parse` per helper
call adds significant subprocess overhead, and `git diff --cached
--name-only` without `--no-renames` can collapse a staged deletion
outside `third_party/protobuf/` paired with an identical file inside it
into a single destination path.

Build the baseline git fixtures once per test class in `setUpClass` and
copy them per test method in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf_test.py`, allow
`_ResolveCheckoutPaths` and `LoadRollState` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to accept an existing
`_CheckoutPaths`, and pass `--no-renames` in
`_RejectStagedChangesOutsideProtobuf`.

ash: Skip resetting accelerators on login when no overrides exist

AshAcceleratorConfiguration::Initialize() already populates the default
accelerators at startup. When a user logs in without shortcut
customization overrides (and no previous user had overrides), skip
calling ResetAllAccelerators() and ApplyPrefOverrides() in
OnActiveUserPrefServiceChanged() to avoid unregistering and
re-registering all Ash accelerators during login.

Use Abseil flat hash containers in local_search_service

Replaces std::unordered_map and std::unordered_set with
absl::flat_hash_map and absl::flat_hash_set across local_search_service
to improve memory usage and performance.

Uses std::exchange when moving container members to thread tasks to
ensure moved-from Abseil containers are left in a reinitialized empty
state.

ash: Fix dangling id reference in HoldingSpaceKeyedService test

the item is removed. Copy it instead. The use-after-free surfaced
after HoldingSpaceModel::GetItem() switched to std::string_view.

[cc] Add deferred value generators and Blink curve proxy

Add the cc types that resolve an animated value at raster time, and
implement the color curve proxy in Blink. Paint will record a key with
a fallback color, and raster will look up the current value for it.

- DeferredPropertyKey pairs a source ElementId with a
  DeferredPropertyType.
- DeferredValueGenerator stores animation progress and samples only
  when the progress changed. Clearing the progress drops the value, so
  raster keeps the painted fallback.
- DeferredColorValueGenerator samples an AnimationCurveProxy<SkColor4f>,
  which the embedder implements and ref counts across threads.
  GenerateDeferredValueMap() collects sampled values into a
  DeferredValueMap.
- CompositorAnimationColorCurve implements
  cc::AnimationCurveProxy<SkColor4f>. Interpolate() is now const, with
  a relaxed atomic interval cache, so the compositor thread can sample
  it.

Nothing uses these yet, so there is no behavior change.

Revert "[CrOS] Avoid loading TTS engines when indexing settings search"

This reverts commit a787dee2d856fa440607efbe4d88486d77ebe03d.

Reason for revert: Avoiding loading the built-in TTS extensions at
login leaves StartupObserver with no observed WebContents when logging
in without a browser window (e.g. ARC++ test provisioning after OOBE).
On official ChromeOS builds (where ImprovedStartupBestEffortDelay is
disabled by default), AfterStartupTaskUtils stalls for the full 180s
kFailsafeTimeout, blocking BEST_EFFORT UI-thread tasks such as
ArcWallpaperService::GetWallpaper(). This stalls Android SystemUI and
KeyguardService initialization for ~166s and breaks multiple ARC++ CTS
tests (b/577511643).

Fix broken DEPS specific_include_rules regexes in //chrome, //chromeos

Fix two categories of regex mistakes in DEPS specific_include_rules keys
under //chrome and //chromeos:

1. Replace unescaped `\.` in non-raw string literals (e.g. `"foo\.cc"`)
   with `"foo\\.cc"` to eliminate Python `SyntaxWarning: invalid escape
   sequence '\.'` warnings.
2. Replace `"foo\\.*"` (which evaluates to the regex `foo\.*`, matching
   `foo` followed by zero or more literal dots, and only matched files
   by accident because `re.match` performs a prefix match):
   - Use `"foo\\..*"` (regex `foo\..*`) when matching `foo.<ext>`.
   - Use `"foo.*"` where files with a suffix before the extension also
     rely on the rule (`display_info_provider_chromeos_unittest.cc` in
     `chrome/browser/extensions/system_display/DEPS`, and
     `dbus_appmenu_registrar.*` and
     `picture_in_picture_browser_frame_view_*` in
     `chrome/browser/ui/views/frame/DEPS`).

Also escape unescaped `.cc` in an adjacent rule in

parent
0e8ca1327cc42f1ec40dbdd69d4a807df7f7e127 [ diff ] 
Add a long-lived mode to dbus_xdg::Request

Some portal requests, such as org.freedesktop.portal.Inhibit, take
effect when the request is made and last until the Request object is
closed. xdg-desktop-portal emits Response(0) for Inhibit on success but
keeps the Request exported, so dbus_xdg::Request, which stops tracking
a request after any response, would leak the inhibition.

Add Request::CreateLongLived(). A long-lived request runs its callback
on a successful response but stays open until the Request is destroyed,
which calls Close. Failure responses and method call errors end it as
before. Some portals never emit a response for Inhibit (1.0.x, or when
the permission store denies every flag), so the callback may never run.
If the Request is destroyed before the method call returns, Close is
sent once the reply names the request's object path, which also covers
portals older than 0.9 that ignore handle_token.

[WebNN] Show the Compiler target EP device in webnn-internals

For contexts that use the Compiler process, webnn-internals showed the
EP devices the GPU process would select when the Compiler process is
disabled. These are not the device the Compiler process actually uses
for offline compilation, e.g. OV GPU was marked as first selected while
the model was compiled for WebGPU.

Override GetExecutionProvidersInfo() in DispatchContextImplOrt to report
only the target EP device, marked as first selected.

omnibox: Skip redundant LocationBarView updates

During browser window creation and tab switches, `LocationBarView`
triggers multiple redundant `OnChanged()`, `LocationIconView::Update()`,
and `OmniboxView::TextChanged()` passes within a single update cycle.

This CL introduces `omnibox::kOmniboxSkipRedundantLocationBarUpdates` to
coalesce redundant location bar and omnibox updates during startup and
tab changes.

Pinpoint Crossbench `browser-startup` A/B results (P50 (median) paired
delta, 95% CI):
- `linux-r350-perf`: `ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint` -5.0 ms /
  -1.48% ([-9.5, -1.5] ms; `newtab`: -10.0 ms / -2.98%),
  `BrowserWindow.FirstPaint` -2.0 ms / -0.79% ([-4.0, +0.0] ms).
- `win-10-perf`: `ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint` -14.0 ms / -0.84%
  ([-32.0, +1.0] ms; Warm: -16.5 ms / -1.00%),
  `BrowserWindow.FirstPaint` -10.0 ms / -0.76% ([-20.0, +3.0] ms).
- `mac-m1-pro-perf`: `FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3` -3.0 ms / -0.70%
  ([-7.0, +0.0] ms), `FirstPaint` & `ReloadButton.FCP` +0.0 ms.

Disable tabs in Cobr tab picker when input limits reached

Updates the tab picker to observe InputState from the searchbox
composebox proxy and disable unselected tab options when browser tab
inputs are disabled or the maximum total inputs limit is reached.

Additionally, updates ContextualTasksExtensionHandler to notify the
InputStateModel when tab context is attached or removed so the input
state stays in sync.

ash: Stop 214 files from compiling the 1.6 MB concierge proto header

In a ChromeOS Chrome build, 214 of the 405 files that include
concierge_client.h no longer compile the generated
concierge_service.pb.h (1.6 MB). On 50 sampled files, compile time fell
0.61 s per file (6.2%) and peak memory 2.7%: about 2.2 CPU-minutes per
full build.

concierge_client.h needed the proto only to name request, response and
signal types. It now forward-declares them, and the .cc files that use
the protos include the header directly.

Test: autoninja chrome unit_tests, gn check, checkdeps.

[focusgroupV2] Add V2 associated-control utilities

Adds utility contracts for effective itemcontrols ownership, associated
linear-item lookup, active-item derivation, and owner-local segment
barrier detection. Keep nested focusgroups, top-layer scopes, and
flat-tree ownership as independent boundaries.

Cover deep and direct controls, nearest-item selection, negative
tabindex, controls without items, nested owners, popovers, slots,
fallback content, and unassociated barriers without wiring navigation
behavior.

Explainer: https://open-ui.org/components/focusgroup-v2.explainer/#item-controls

[chromecast] Fix CastWebContentsActivity preemption race condition

When a CastWebContentsActivity is finishing (for example, when a delayed
teardown or stop intent triggers mIsFinishingState), calling
finishAndRemoveTask() marks the Activity as finishing, and the
subsequent onStop() lifecycle callback invokes
mIsFinishingState.set("User exit") with a different reason string.
Because Controller.set() only deduplicates identical values,
mIsFinishingState activated a second time and called
finishAndRemoveTask() again, causing a "Duplicate finish request" race
condition in WindowManager during LAUNCH_SINGLE_INSTANCE task
replacement.

Add Observer.once() to adapt an Observer so that it opens at most once,
route the !CastBrowserHelper.isBrowserInitialized() early abort through
mIsFinishingState.set(), and wrap the mIsFinishingState subscriber in
Observer.once().

Bug: b:539396548, b:552595895
Test: cast_base_junit_tests --gtest_filter="*ObserverTest*"
Test: cast_shell_junit_tests --gtest_filter="*CastWebContentsActivityTest*"

[NTP] Lazy load voice search, action chips, and customize buttons

Voice search, animated glow, action chips, the doodle share dialog, and
the customize buttons are not needed on initial paint (they are only
active after user interaction or rendered inside lazyRender_), but their
code was pulled into shared.rollup.js on the initial critical path via
eager imports and shared enums.

This CL:

- Moves VoiceAction, VoiceError, and recordVoiceAction() to
  metrics_utils.ts, moves ActionChipsRetrievalState to
  action_chips_proxy.ts, and removes the unused cr_auto_img.js import
  from composebox_tab_favicon.ts.

- Moves the voice search, animated glow, action chips, customize
  buttons, and doodle share dialog imports to lazy_load.ts and
  new_tab_page_eager.ts.

- Awaits ensureLazyLoaded() before flipping lazyRender_ = true in
  AppElement.firstUpdated(), when opening voice or Lens search in
  AppElement.openVoiceSearch_() / onOpenLensSearch_(), and when opening
  the doodle share dialog in LogoElement.onShareButtonClick_() (with a
  no-op ensureLazyLoaded() override in new_tab_page_extension).

- Adds NewTabPageLazyLoadBrowserTest.LazyLoad (lazy_load_test.ts) to
  verify the exact custom elements defined by new_tab_page.js (26 eager
  elements) vs. lazy_load.js (52 lazy elements).

With optimize_webui=true, enabling kNtpLazyLoadComposebox shrinks the
initial critical-path JS (new_tab_page.rollup.js + shared.rollup.js) by
-12.8% (-164.2 KB), for a cumulative reduction of -27.0% (-413.7 KB).

webnn: let the GPU process terminate a misbehaving Compiler process

This CL adds a `WebNNCompilerHost` mojo interface to let the GPU process
ask the browser to terminate the Compiler process when it sent a model
buffer that violated the expected contract.

The GPU process creates the `WebNNCompilerHost` pipe itself and passes
the receiver to `RequestCompilerContext()` alongside the existing
CompilerContext/ModelLoader pipes. In the browser, each Compiler process
is now managed by a `CompilerHostImpl` that owns both the remote to the
Compiler process and the set of `WebNNCompilerHost` receivers.

On the ORT backend, only genuine contract violations (invalid session
metadata, invalid protobuf format) trigger Terminate(), ordinary runtime
errors only report a compilation failure.

[Net] Fix and re-enable ResumeMainJobImmediatelyOnStreamFailed

Fix and re-enable ResumeMainJobImmediatelyOnStreamFailed in
HttpStreamFactoryJobControllerTest, which was disabled in
https://crrev.com/c/1821860

Two changes since the test was written caused it to fail:

1. When https://crrev.com/c/1821860 removed the 1-second
    `QuicConnectionLogger::net_log_is_capturing_timer_` polling timer,
    `EXPECT_NE(0u, GetPendingMainThreadTaskCount)` began failing after
    the alternative job failed. When `ResumeMainJobLater` posts an
    immediate task to resume the main job, it calls
    `resume_main_job_callback_.Reset`, which cancels the previously
    posted 15us delayed task.
    `TaskQueueImpl::MoveReadyDelayedTasksToWorkQueue` sweeps canceled
    tasks from the front of the delayed incoming queue, so no pending
    main-thread tasks remain once the immediate task runs (the previous
    non-zero count came solely from the unrelated `QuicConnectionLogger`
    timer). Update the expectation to
    `EXPECT_EQ(0u, GetPendingMainThreadTaskCount)`.

2. While the test was disabled, https://crrev.com/c/4250743 made QUIC
   session
    creation asynchronous (`WaitForQuicSessionCreation`) and
    https://crrev.com/c/4368358 gated that behavior behind
    `features::kAsyncQuicSession` (enabled by default on Windows). When
    `kAsyncQuicSession` is enabled, `Job::OnQuicSessionCreated`—which
    calls `JobController::OnConnectionInitialized` to unblock
    `main_job_` and post the 15us `ResumeMainJobLater` task—runs on a
    zero-delay posted task rather than synchronously inside
    `job_controller_->Start`. Call `FastForwardBy(`base::TimeDelta`)`
    after `Start` so the zero-delay session creation task runs before
    asserting
   `!`JobControllerPeer::main_job_is_blocked`(job_controller_)`.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Remove the Linux frame touch-hold data drag suppression

WindowEventFilterLinux tracked a touch pressed on the caption or a
resize border and held a
DesktopDragDropClientOzone::ScopedSuppressForWindowMove() scope until
that touch ended, to keep a compromised renderer from latching a touch
data drag onto the user's touch (bug 574902935).

WebContentsViewAura::StartDragging now requires a renderer-initiated
touch drag to be backed by an unused touch that was pressed on the web
contents itself, which a touch on the frame never is. That makes the
suppression redundant, so remove it along with its tests.

Remove the Linux caption click-hold data drag suppression

WindowEventFilterLinux armed a
DesktopDragDropClientOzone::ScopedSuppressForWindowMove() scope while
the left button was held on the caption, to keep a compromised renderer
from latching a data drag onto the user's held button (bug 553151406).
The suppression had to be released in sync with the click-hold, and bug
576129254 showed it could be released early by a renderer-manufactured
crossing event.

WebContentsViewAura::StartDragging now requires the left button press to
have been dispatched to the web contents itself, which a caption press
(or a press on a draggable region of a frameless app window) never is.
That makes the suppression redundant, so remove it. Clearing aura::Env's
button state when a move is handed off to the window manager is kept,
since the window manager may consume the button release.

The click-hold interactive UI test no longer checks the suppression, but
still checks the threshold hand-off and the button state.

[iOS] Re-enable `DedicatedWebTransportHttp3Test.CloseTimeout`

Re-enable `DedicatedWebTransportHttp3Test.CloseTimeout` on iOS, where it
was disabled for flakiness in https://crrev.com/c/3741068

The underlying flakiness was caused by `CreateQuicSimpleServerSocket` in
`net/tools/quic/quic_simple_server_socket.cc` calling
`socket->AllowAddressReuse` (`SO_REUSEADDR`) unconditionally when
binding `QuicSimpleServer` to ephemeral port 0 (`[::]:0`). On BSD/Darwin
(macOS and iOS), `SO_REUSEADDR` on an ephemeral port allows concurrent
test processes to bind to the exact same UDP port and intercept or drop
each other's packets during the test.

This bug was repaired in https://crrev.com/c/8266656, which updated
`CreateQuicSimpleServerSocket` to only call `AllowAddressReuse` when
`address.port != 0`, ensuring each `QuicSimpleServer` instance gets a
unique ephemeral port.

Re-enables the `DedicatedWebTransportHttp3Test.CloseTimeout` unit test
on iOS.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

migrating them away from RunUntilIdle() and toward targeted
synchronization with APIs such as RunUntil(), TestFuture, RunLoop
callbacks, observer waiters, or exact mock-time advancement.

mounter. The late filesystem mount response posts MountPoint's
weak-bound completion on the same sequence before the reply is queued.
This keeps the callback and unmount expectations active through that
completion without draining unrelated tasks.

[basic process] Prepare the API shim for multi-process audits

Lets apifw.dll audit long, parallel workloads such as Blink web tests:

- --basic-process-api-test-log-dir writes one log per process into an
  existing directory and enables audit, call-site and log-once modes.
- --basic-process-api-test-log-once logs each distinct stub record once
  per process.
- Log deduplication uses an open-addressing set of 64-bit key hashes,
  every record ends with a newline, and tripwire stacks use module+RVA
  frames like call-site stacks.
- More APIs reached by renderers are logged and forwarded during audits
  instead of hitting the tripwire, including the Winsock event APIs.
- The no-CRT runtime moves into shim/, libc++ hardening support is
  centralized in libcxx_support.h, and shared allocation-free string
  helpers are covered by sbox_unittests.

Mojo C++: Take interfaces & handles directly into stub parameters

Shrinks Android arm32 size by 22kb.

Generated stubs, response callbacks, and StructTraits::Read() took
interface and handle fields via:
  p_foo = input_data_view.TakeFoo<decltype(p_foo)>();

which constructs a temporary, move-assigns it, and then destroys the
temporary. This adds DataView overloads of TakeFoo() that take an
output parameter, so that generated code can deserialize directly into
the (default-constructed) destination.

Mojo C++: Validate non-nullable fields with a single call

Shrinks Android arm32 size by 20kb.

Generated Validate() functions validated each non-nullable pointer,
handle, or interface field with two calls: one to check that it is not
null (e.g. ValidatePointerNonNullable()), and one to validate its
contents (e.g. ValidateContainer()).

This adds ValidateNonNullContainer(), ValidateNonNullStruct(),
ValidateNonNullNonInlinedUnion(), and ValidateNonNullHandleOrInterface(),
which take the field index and also perform the null check, so that
generated code needs only a single call per field.

[ash] Create Profiles at the User's path in Personalization tests

In production, the Profile for a User is placed at
<user_data_dir>/u-${username_hash}. However, some Personalization app
unittests created TestingProfiles at paths that do not match the User:

- PersonalizationAppWallpaperProviderImplTest passed
  BrowserContextHelper::GetUserBrowserContextDirName(username_hash) as
  the profile name. TestingProfileManager treats it as a user name and
  hashes it again, so the Profile was created at an unrelated path
  (u-u-...-hash-hash).
- PersonalizationAppSeaPenProviderImplTest took the profile name
  separately from the AccountId, and some tests passed a name that does
  not correspond to the User (e.g. for child and demo mode public
  accounts).

This CL creates the Profiles from the email of the AccountId, so that
they are placed at the path for the User, as same as production. The
redundant `name` parameter is removed from SetUpProfileForTesting().

This is a preparation to check consistency between the User and the
Profile path.

ash: Pass VariationsService* to FeatureAccessChecker

Replace FeatureAccessChecker::VariationsServiceCallback (introduced in
https://crrev.com/c/6171785) with a VariationsService* parameter across
FeatureAccessChecker and its callers:

- LobsterServiceProvider::BuildInstanceFor
    -> LobsterService
    -> LobsterSystemStateProviderImpl
    -> FeatureAccessChecker
- ScannerKeyedServiceFactory::BuildInstanceFor
    -> ScannerKeyedService
    -> FeatureAccessChecker
- ChromeMediaAppGuestUIDelegate::GetFeatureAccessChecker
    -> FeatureAccessChecker

FeatureAccessChecker now implements VariationsService::Observer
(https://crrev.com/c/8267742) and resets its variations_service_ pointer
in OnVariationsServiceDestroyed() so it does not dangle when
VariationsService is destroyed before KeyedServices during
BrowserProcessImpl::StartTearDown().

its Finch params: ZSSMaxRecentPages (default 15), ZSSMaxRecentDuration

[Feed] Avoid waiting for scroll restore when NTP has no scroll offset

During NTP creation, FeedSurfaceMediator#updateContent() calls
setupHeaders() (which synchronously invokes restoreSavedInstanceState())
and then bindStream(). Previously:
1. bindStream() unconditionally overwrote RestoringState with
   WAITING_TO_RESTORE, clobbering NO_STATE_TO_RESTORE when no scroll
   state existed.
2. Navigating away from an unscrolled NTP saved position=0, offset=0,
   which set WAITING_TO_RESTORE even though no scroll event fires at the
   top of the list.

Both cases caused NtpSmoothTransitionDelegate to keep the NTP at alpha=0
upon back navigation until the 1000ms fallback timeout expired.

Treat null, NO_POSITION, and (position == 0 && offset == 0) as
NO_STATE_TO_RESTORE, and only set WAITING_TO_RESTORE in bindStream()
when there is a scroll position to restore.

R=hanxi@chromium.org

[WebUI Toolbar] Align WebUI omnibox drops with the native omnibox

Adds browser tests for dropping into the WebUI omnibox. They cover text,
URLs, files, javascript: and chrome:// URLs, dragged from a web page or
from another application, and check the results against the native Views
omnibox on Linux. Like the native omnibox, a drop replaces the omnibox
text and selects all of it, without opening the popup or navigating.

URL drops now work like they do for the home button and the toolbar:
- A new OmniboxActionDropUrl carries the dropped text/uri-list URL.
OmniboxActionDropText is now only used for plain text.
- WebUIToolbarDragState captures the drag's first URL before
FilterDropData. WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::OnDropUrl() prefers that URL,
which is the one the native omnibox sees, and strips javascript: schemes
from it like OmniboxViewViews::PerformDrop() does.
- The WebUI forwards the text/uri-list URL as is, and no longer recovers
it from text/plain.

NavigationCounter now only counts primary main frame navigations. The
New Tab page, which the empty omnibox tests start from, loads subframes
on its own, e.g. the One Google Bar.

mahi: Remove g_browser_process from CanUseMahiService

Inject VariationsService into ash::mahi_availability::CanUseMahiService
and ash::mahi_availability::IsMahiAvailable instead of reading
g_browser_process->variations_service() directly.

ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsAsh
  +-> ash::MagicBoostState
  |     +-> ash::mahi_availability::IsMahiAvailable
  |           +-> ash::mahi_availability::CanUseMahiService
  +-> ash::MahiManagerImpl
        +-> ash::mahi_availability::IsMahiAvailable
              +-> ash::mahi_availability::CanUseMahiService

Both MagicBoostState and MahiManagerImpl are owned by
ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsAsh and destroyed in PostMainMessageLoopRun
before BrowserProcessImpl::StartTearDown() destroys VariationsService,
so they hold a non-null raw_ref<const variations::VariationsService>.

Also remove the browser_process dependency from
chrome/browser/ash/mahi/BUILD.gn and chrome/browser/ash/mahi/DEPS, and
set up TestVariationsService in MagicBoostState and MahiManagerImpl
unit test fixtures.

login: Inject LoginDisplayHost dependencies into SwitchWebUItoMojo()

SwitchWebUItoMojo() reads local_state, metrics_service,
application_locale_storage, shared_url_loader_factory and
browser_policy_connector_ash from g_browser_process and passes them to
ShowLoginWizard(). Take them as parameters instead, and remove its
TODO(crbug.com/403154552). Its two callers, WizardController's
OnEnrollmentDone() and OnDemoSetupScreenExit(), pass their injected
members. In production these are the same process-wide objects that
SwitchWebUItoMojo() used to read, so this doesn't change behavior.

WizardController's metrics_service_ may be null in unit tests, so it is
CHECKed right before it is passed on. The factory is copied rather than
moved: when the login screen locale has to be switched first, the
WizardController outlives the call and may still use it. In
WizardControllerDemoSetupTest.OnlineDemoSetupFlowFinished, the
LoginDisplayHostMojo created after the switch now gets the test
URLLoaderFactory that the fixture sets on the WizardController.

login_display_host_webui.cc no longer uses GetFeatures(), so drop its
global_features.h include and DEPS entry.

Dependency injection flow:
  ChromeSessionManager::Initialize
  +--> StartLoginOobeSession
       +--> ShowLoginWizard
            +--> LoginDisplayHostWebUI
                 +--> WizardController
                      +--> SwitchWebUItoMojo
                           +--> ShowLoginWizard
                                +--> LoginDisplayHostMojo

[SensitiveContent] Fix WindowAndroid detach and async polling in tests

In SensitiveContentTest#testSwapViewAndroidDelegate, passing null as the
WindowAndroid argument to WebContents#setDelegates cleared the top-level
native window while TabImpl.mIsDetachedFromActivity remained false. When
the 3-second transient browser-controls token expired on tablet builders
before the next batched test's resetTabStateThorough() ran, creating the
new tab triggered an AssertionError in TabImpl#isDetachedFromActivity.
Additionally, assertSensitive and assertNotSensitive checked the
ContentView sensitivity synchronously after page load, racing against
asynchronous Autofill form classification.

Pass the activity's WindowAndroid in testSwapViewAndroidDelegate, wait
for initial sensitivity before swapping delegates, and poll on the UI
thread in assertSensitive and assertNotSensitive.

Validation: flake SensitiveContentTest#testSwapViewAndroidDelegate failed 2/20 without this change, 0/20 with it on android_35_google_apis_tablet_x64_tablet_landscape_local

Fix style invalidation for moveBefore of slotted nodes

When a slotted element (either assigned or fallback) moves between
the slot element and the shadow-host in a way that does not change
the element's flat tree parent, two things go wrong:

- The code that tries to avoid style invalidations during a
state-preserving move is based on stale slot assignments, and fails
to apply necessary style invalidations. Fixed by loosening the
conditions for calling ParentSlotChanged() in
HTMLSlotElement::UpdateFlatTreeNodeDataForAssignedNodes.

- The IsInCanvasSubtree flag is cleared aggressively when the element
is removed but is not properly re-applied upon insertion because
FlatTreeParentChanged() is skipped (because the element's flat tree
parent did not change). Fixed by tracking whether a slot element is
displaying active fallback or assigned nodes in
HTMLSlotElement::flat_tree_children_are_fallback_, and calling
ParentSlotChanged() unconditionally when it toggles.

[build] Enable Siso racing and local linking on *-build-service

The Chrome Build Service prototype builders run on high-spec C4D VMs
with local NVMe SSDs (c4d-standard-384-lssd on Linux and
c4d-standard-192-lssd on Windows). On these machines, linking locally
and racing local compiles against RBE avoids waiting on RBE link workers
and downloading multi-GB linked binaries back from CAS.

Drop "remote-link" from siso_configs on both linux-build-service and
win-build-service so C++ archives, shared libraries, and executables
link locally, and add "racing" to siso_experiments on
linux-build-service. Leave "racing" off win-build-service for now
because Siso's runStrategy dispatches to runRacing before checking
per-rule strict_remote, which clang-cl/cxx_module needs on Windows hosts
so backslash paths in local .pcm files do not break downstream remote
Linux compiles (https://crbug.com/477762548).

[Enterprise] Implement policy::GetMachineName() on Android

On Android, policy::GetMachineName() (and transitively
policy::GetDeviceName() and policy::GetBrowserDeviceIdentifier())
previously returned an empty string because POSIX gethostname(2) always
returns "localhost" on Android.

Implement policy::GetMachineName() on Android behind a default-on
killswitch (kReportAndroidMachineName) so enterprise reporting, security
signals collection, and managed client certificate provisioning receive
the Android device name. Resolution queries
base::android::device_info::device_name() (Settings.Global.DEVICE_NAME)
first and falls back to base::android::android_info::model()
(android.os.Build.MODEL) when unset or empty.

Also catch Exception in DeviceInfo.getDeviceName() so custom OEM
SettingsProvider exceptions fall back to Build.MODEL instead of causing
uncaught JNI exceptions, and update AndroidSignalsCollector to call
policy::GetDeviceName().

ash: Stop 1494 files from compiling quick_pair_mediator.h via shell.h

In a ChromeOS Chrome build, 1,494 of the 2,061 files that include
ash/shell.h no longer compile quick_pair_mediator.h and the Bluetooth
mojom bindings it pulls in. On 50 sampled files, compile time fell
0.34 s per file (3.7%) and peak memory 3.2%: about 8 CPU-minutes per
full build.

shell.h included that header only because the private Shell::Init()
took a nested Mediator::Factory, which can't be forward-declared.
Init() now takes the ShellInitParams that CreateInstance() already
gets. Behavior is unchanged.

Test: autoninja chrome ash_unittests ash_webui_unittests, gn check.

optimization_guide: prune unused includes and deps from features

Remove unused #include directives from optimization_guide_features.{cc,h}
(replace net/base/url_util.h with url/url_constants.h for
url::kHttpsScheme) and drop the corresponding unused dependencies
(//components/variations, //net, //third_party/metrics_proto, //ui/base)
from //components/optimization_guide/core:features.

Because GN propagates .harddeps across all deps of a component, dropping
these unused dependencies avoids propagating //ui/base, //net, and
//components/variations compile-time and link-time dependencies to
upstream targets depending on :features.

[GMC] Show Stop Casting for Remote Playback and Mirroring on ChromeOS

crrev.com/c/8462845 switched the ChromeOS GMC to the modern cast footer
for local media sessions, but the footer was still not built on
ChromeOS for media routes started from tabs.

First, GetSessionRoute() bailed out unless kFallbackToAudioTabMirroring
was enabled or HasRemotePlaybackRoute() returned true. Both
kFallbackToAudioTabMirroring and kMediaRemotingWithoutFullscreen were
disabled by default on ChromeOS. Local media sessions with an active
Remote Playback or Tab Mirroring route (e.g. history.com, ted.com)
never matched a route, so no stop callback or footer was built.

Second, kFallbackToAudioTabMirroring was originally disabled on
ChromeOS (crbug.com/302012982) only because GMC could not stop
mirroring routes at the time, which crrev.com/c/8462845 fixed.

This CL:
- Associates both Remote Playback and Tab Mirroring routes with the
  media session of the tab that started them in GetSessionRoute(),
  regardless of feature flags, so active routes can always be stopped.
- Enables kFallbackToAudioTabMirroring by default on all platforms,
  including ChromeOS.
- Derives the cast mode for metrics from the route's media source rather
  than session metadata, and removes HasRemotePlaybackRoute().
- Removes the feature gate in HasTabMirroringSessionForWebContents().
- Updates ChromeOS browser tests and unit tests to run with default
  features, enables CastDeviceListHostTest.StartAudioTabMirroring on
  ChromeOS, and verifies that the stop casting footer displays even if
  fallback to audio tab mirroring is disabled.

R=steimel@chromium.org

WebUILocationBar: Fix ZoomViewInteractiveUiTest

Two issues caused ZoomViewInteractiveUiTest.
ShowAndHideZoomBubbleByClickWithMouse to fail or flake, particularly
when WebUILocationBar is enabled:

1. DoZoomIn() calls SetZoomLevel(content::PAGE_ZOOM_IN), which opens an
automatic notification bubble with a 1500ms auto-close timer. In native
Views, ZoomView::Update() schedules a layout invalidation that runs
while MoveMouseTo() pumps the UI loop, triggering
LocationBarView::OnBoundsChanged() and closing the automatic bubble
before ClickMouse() runs. With WebUILocationBar, the zoom icon lives in
WebUI so no native Views layout invalidation closes the bubble, and on
slow bots the 1500ms timer can also expire right before click 2.
Because the click suppression threshold was zeroed up front, widget
deactivation on click did not prevent the click from immediately
re-opening the bubble. Fix this by suppressing the automatic
notification bubble during the initial SetZoomLevel() call, explicitly
laying out the root view after the icon becomes visible, and keeping
the default click suppression threshold active until after the dismiss
click hides the bubble.

2. When the zoom bubble shows or hides, TrackedElementHandler sends
OnElementHighlightChanged() over the TrackedElementManager Mojo pipe
while ClickMouse() dispatches native mouse events over the input pipe.
If a highlight update is still in flight when the next mouse click
runs, the WebUI button's highlight state and suppression window can be
out of sync. Fix this by polling ZoomAccessor().HasIconHighlight() ==
visible alongside bubble visibility in WaitForZoomBubble().

[Color] Memoize ColorMixer results and optimize ColorProvider map

Introduces features::kThemeChangeOptimizationV2 and optimizes
ColorProvider generation and lookup:

- Memoizes intermediate ColorMixer::GetResultColor() evaluations on the
  head input mixer when kThemeChangeOptimizationV2 is enabled, hosting
  the cache on ColorProvider (sharing ColorProvider::color_map_ directly
  when no postprocessing mixers are present) to avoid repeated DAG
  re-evaluation of shared color tokens across ColorTransform steps.

- Switches ColorProvider::ColorMap from std::map to base::flat_map for
  cache-friendly contiguous color lookups.

- Deduplicates repeated fg.Run() and bg.Run() evaluations in
  AdjustHighlightColorForContrast().

Fix UAF in FloatedWindowInfo on size constraints change

When a floated window's size constraints change such that it can no
longer be floated, OnResizabilityOrSizeConstraintsChanged()
synchronously unfloats the window and destroys the FloatedWindowInfo
instance.

Updating last_minimum_size_ and last_maximum_size_ after this call
caused a heap-use-after-free. This updates those member variables before
calling OnResizabilityOrSizeConstraintsChanged(), and adds a regression
test.

BUG=b:502082819
TEST=WindowFloatTest

e10a6dabc2d16cecba34a899c76d29b787e5eeb4 [ diff ] 
Fix use-after-free in TrustStoreWin certificate store monitoring

Event-driven Windows certificate store monitoring was previously added
to the Windows trust store, but it refreshes the stores by issuing
CERT_STORE_CTRL_RESYNC against the live HCERTSTOREs that are already
published to readers. Because the TrustStoreWin is a process-global
that is read without any lock by every certificate verification thread,
te resync mutates the collection store's internal list while it's
walking it on other threads. This causes a UAF within crypt32 and the
cause of sporadic crashes.

This change redesigns the trust store around an immutable snapshot
instead of in-place mutation:

- Impl is now RefCountedThreadSafe and const after construction. Readers
  take a scoped_refptr<const Impl> for the duration of the call, so a
  concurrent refresh is invisible to them and the stores they are
  enumerating stay alive until they are done.
- A refresh builds a brand new Impl and publishes it with an atomic swap
  under impl_lock_, with rebuild_lock_ serializing builders. Nothing that
  is already visible to a reader is ever modified.
- A single ref-counted ChangeMonitor owns the change event, the
  base::win::ObjectWatcher and the staleness flag. Every Impl registered
  for notifications holds a reference to it, which makes the lifetime
  ordering structural: the event cannot be closed while any Impl is still
  registered against it. ChangeMonitor is a
  RefCountedDeleteOnSequence so the final destruction (and therefore
  ObjectWatcher::StopWatching()) always happens on the watch sequence,
  even when the last reference is dropped on a verifier thread.
- The watch is re-armed immediately in OnObjectSignaled(), before the
  debounce timer is restarted, and the staleness flag is cleared before
  the rebuild rather than after. A change racing a rebuild now costs at
  most one redundant rebuild instead of being dropped.
- Store changes are debounced (1s) so that a single policy update does not
  trigger several rebuilds; previously the burst coalescing happened by
  accident because the wait was not re-armed.
- ApplyCertStoreControlToAllStores() now attempts every store and
  aggregates the result.

The net result of this redesign is that during a swap, two generations
of stores are briefly alive, and a store change now rebuilds the stores
rather than resyncing them in place. Both happen off the hot path, on
the monitoring sequence, and are bounded by the debounce interval.

The change adds two bot-runnable regression tests:
TrustStoreWinTest.StoreChangeEventTriggersRefresh covers the lost-change
race by signaling the change event twice and requiring a notification
each time, and TrustStoreWinTest.ConcurrentReadsDuringRefresh exercises
reads on four threads against repeated refreshes, which is the case that
reproduces the use-after-free under ASAN. Neither test mutates the OS
certificate stores. The existing MANUAL_AutoSyncCertStores test is
updated to describe the new mechanism.

*This change was coauthored by an AI agent.*

[ContextualTasks] Drop iframe message fallback

`ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData::PostSearchMessage` previously fell
back to broadcasting `ClientToSearchMessage` payloads across extension
frames that had completed a per-frame `postMessage` handshake when no
Service Worker channel was connected. Now that search messaging routes
exclusively through `ContextualTasksExtensionServiceWorkerHandler`, the
iframe broadcast fallback and per-frame handshake tracking
(`handshake_completed_frame_tokens_`) are obsolete and can be removed so
outbound messages dispatch solely through the Service Worker callback.

[sbom-quality] Generate README.chromium when making jdk CIPD package

The path to the LICENSE file can vary depending on the platform (i.e.
linux-amd64 vs mac-arm64). This CL updates the 3pp.py script to generate
the README.chromium with the version and path to license file.

The checked-in README.chromium at third_party/jdk/README.chromium will
be removed in a following CL, so that the metadata file is only on disk
when the CIPD package is actually on disk too.

[Focus] Fix Non-Group Focus Mode Dissolution and Group Commands

- Dissolve the focused ephemeral group in TabStripModel::EnterFocusMode
  when switching focus directly to another tab group.
- Make CloseTabGroup / CloseAllTabsInGroup a no-op for ephemeral tab
  groups to prevent crashing on IDC_CLOSE_TAB_GROUP.
- Treat ephemeral groups as ungrouped in WillContextMenuGroup and
  validate IDC_GROUP_TARGET_TAB on macOS so Group Tab toggles into a
  new permanent tab group.

Optimize and modernize container operations in local_search_service.

This change updates container operations across local search service
components:
- Use try_emplace, insert_or_assign, and structured bindings to
  eliminate redundant lookups in maps.
- Replace manual iteration and deletion loops with std::erase_if.
- Reserve capacity and use emplace_back / std::move to avoid unnecessary
  allocations and copies in test helpers.
- Clean up index initialization and error handling in
  LocalSearchService.

[TWA] Add metrics for waiting for service worker for share target

Records how a POST Web Share Target delivered to a TWA or WebAPK is
handled by PendingShareTargetPost when waiting for the app's service
worker:

- WebApp.ShareTarget.WaitForServiceWorker.Outcome: whether the POST
  was sent (service worker already registered, service worker without
  a fetch handler, origin has another registration, service worker
  activated, bootstrap failed, timed out, service worker context
  destroyed) or dropped (browser-initiated navigation, newer share,
  direct share target POST, maximum wait reached on another origin,
  WebContents destroyed). Recorded once per share, when
  PendingShareTargetPost is destroyed.
- WebApp.ShareTarget.WaitForServiceWorker.TimeToActivation: time from
  starting to load the start URL until the service worker activated and
  the POST was sent, including any time spent on another origin.

These show how often the bootstrap path is taken, how often it times
out, and whether the timeout value is appropriate.

[omnibox] Add Full WebUI popup keyboard traversal interactive tests.

This CL adds parameterized interactive UI tests (Views and WebUI
toolbars) that drive the Full WebUI omnibox popup with real key presses
(SendKeyPress) to close testing gaps identified during an audit.

- FullWebUIOmniboxTabTraversalInteractiveTest
  .TabTraversesAllPopupElementsForward and
  .ShiftTabTraversesAllPopupElementsBackward: walk five matches forward
  (Tab) and backward (Shift+Tab), including the AIM button,
  remove-suggestion buttons and a Switch-to-Tab action chip, and wrap
  around in both directions. Each stop checks the WebUI selection, the
  input's fill text, AIM button visibility and the browser-side
  OmniboxEditModel selection. Catches elements skipped or visited out of
  order, broken wrap-around, AIM button / remove / action buttons
  dropping out of the tab order, and the WebUI and browser selections
  disagreeing. The AIM button focused alongside a match is checked on
  the WebUI side only, since SearchboxHandler::SetPopupSelection() does
  not forward that state to the edit model.

- ShiftTabExitsKeywordModeEnteredViaTab: Shift+Tab leaves keyword mode
  entered with Tab on the keyword chip, and restores the default match
  and typed text. Catches Shift+Tab failing to leave keyword mode.

- ArrowUpAndDownWrapAroundAndMirrorInput: ArrowDown / ArrowUp move by
  whole lines (skipping buttons), wrap at both ends, and mirror each
  match's text into the input. Catches broken wrap-around, arrows
  landing on buttons, and stale input text.

- ArrowLeftAndRightCharacterAndWordMovement: character movement, word
  movement with Ctrl (Option on macOS) + Left/Right, and collapsing a
  full selection with plain Left/Right. Catches the popup's key handling
  swallowing or misrouting caret-movement keys.

- FullWebUIOmniboxZpsInteractiveTest:
  - ZpsShownOnFocus: ZPS opens on focus on the NTP, with an empty input.
  - DoubleEscapeFromZpsMatchThenArrowDownReopensZps: from a highlighted
    ZPS match, ESC #1 reverts the input with the dropdown open, ESC #2
    closes the dropdown, and ArrowDown reopens ZPS.
  - DoubleEscapeFromTypedQueryThenArrowDownReopensZps: from a typed
    query, ESC #1 closes the dropdown, ESC #2 clears the input, and
    ArrowDown reopens ZPS. Catches ZPS not opening on focus, ESC not
    reverting, closing or clearing, focus being lost, and ArrowDown no
    longer querying ZPS when the dropdown is closed.

[History] Make history list collapsible by day and website

Previously, browsing multi-day history in chrome://history required
scrolling past all entries in every date card and every repeated visit
to the same domain. This change adds header collapse toggles to date
cards using cr-collapse so entire days can be collapsed or expanded, and
adds domain-level collapse toggles on the first entry of repeated visits
to the same domain within a day while keeping card boundaries, time-gap
separators, and viewport auto-loading accurate.

Walkthrough & screenshots: https://crbug.com/40332037#comment56

Integrate Linux web app shortcuts with DynamicLauncherPortal

Integrates DynamicLauncherPortal with web_app_shortcut_linux.cc to
dynamically create, update, and uninstall Linux web app shortcuts. This
is required in sandboxes such as Flatpak, where Chromium can't write
host .desktop files.

Key implementation details:
- Feature flag kWebAppsUseDynamicLauncherPortal disabled by default and
  declared in web_app_shortcut_linux.h for Finch rollout. The portal is
  only used inside Flatpak (base::nix::GetAppSandbox()). Host installs
  keep writing .desktop files directly, and so do snaps, since the
  DynamicLauncher portal doesn't support them
  (https://github.com/flatpak/xdg-desktop-portal/issues/2014).
- If the portal's Install call fails, falls back to the legacy install
  and records the new kPortalInstallFailed bucket of
  Apps.CreateShortcuts.Linux.Result.
- FinalizeInstallOrUpdateJob asks the user to approve the launcher via
  PrepareInstall before committing user installs, and aborts with
  kUserInstallDeclined if the portal dialog is cancelled.
- Silent manifest updates skip the portal preflight, since they can't
  show a dialog. Without a portal token, an existing portal-installed
  launcher is left untouched instead of being replaced by a legacy one.
  Apps without a portal launcher keep using the legacy path.
- Handles portal-prefixed desktop file IDs in shortcut location queries
  and profile shortcut file searches, preventing double-prefixing.
- Strips Name=, Icon=, Actions=, and non-[Desktop Entry] groups when
  constructing portal desktop file content to satisfy portal single-group
  validation.
- Handles portal shortcut uninstallation with legacy fallback to cleanly
  remove portal-owned and legacy launchers even during portal unavailability
  or feature rollback.
- Runs update-desktop-database after portal installation to refresh MIME
  and protocol handler caches.
- Passes editable_name=false in PrepareInstall options to prevent user
  renaming desynchronization.
- GetShortcutIconBytes picks the icon with gfx::ImageFamily::GetBest()
  and downscales it to at most 512px.

[Clank] Add disabled commit tests for Omnibox minimization

Behind ClankOmniboxSameOriginMinimization, a navigation that starts as
same-origin while the Omnibox is offscreen may redirect before
committing, fail with an error page, finish without committing (e.g.
HTTP 204 or download), or have the Omnibox revealed by the user before
commit.

Land @DisabledTest unit tests defining the commit-time verification
rules ahead of the implementation (re-checking origin at commit,
snapping the Omnibox visible without animation on cross-origin
redirects, keeping controls hidden on A->B->A redirects or non-committed
navigations, and checking each overlapping navigation at commit). These
disabled tests will be enabled by the implementation CL.

The existing NavigationHandle.createForTesting() overloads hardcode
navigationId = 0 and isHistory/isBack/isForward = false, so tests cannot
model overlapping or history navigations without Mockito.spy(). Add a
createForTesting() overload that takes these values, and add
NavigationHandleTestBuilder to content_java_test_support so tests set
them by name. The follow-up nav-type tests use the history flags.

Also add callDidRedirectForTesting() and a callDidFinishForTesting()
overload that sets isSameOrigin and isErrorPage, so tests stop calling
the @CalledByNative didRedirect() and didFinish() directly.
callDidFinishForTesting() now keeps the transition from navigation start
instead of resetting it to LINK. All existing callers start with LINK,
so their behavior does not change.

[ContextualTasks] Fix pin IPH trigger for open panel and Lens sessions

Under Pinning V2, the permanent pinning IPH promo
(kIPHSidePanelContextualTasksPinnableFeature) is intended show when side
panel is open and a query has been submitted. However, two issues
prevented the IPH from showing while the side panel was open:

1. Anchor view visibility: The IPH anchors to the ephemeral toolbar
   button (kContextualTasksEphemeralToolbarButtonElementId). Previously,
   the button only showed after closing the side panel because
   ShouldShowEphemeralButton() relied on IsActiveTabEligible(), which is
   only populated during OnEntryWillHide(). Consequently, the IPH could
   not display while the panel was open. In ShouldShowEphemeralButton(),
   ensure the button is visible while the panel is open when Pinning V2
   is active and the button is unpinned (should_show_button |=
   IsPanelOpen()). Notify visibility on panel open/close.

2. Lens entry source suppression: When a user opened Contextual Tasks
   via Lens selection and then submitted a follow-up AIM query, the
   session remained marked as EntrySource::kLensOverlay. In
   CanTriggerPinningPromoForAiPage(), is_lens_overlay_entry skipped
   checking current_task->GetUrlResources(), ignoring the committed
   webpage context and blocking the IPH until the panel was closed and
   reopened. Fix: Remove the is_lens_overlay_entry bypass in
   CanTriggerPinningPromoForAiPage(). Completed AIM queries

Make Linux web app shortcut creation and deletion asynchronous

CreateDesktopShortcut(), UpdateDesktopShortcuts(), DeleteDesktopShortcuts()
and DeleteAllDesktopShortcuts() now report their result through a
base::OnceCallback<void(bool)> instead of a return value. They also
create their own base::Environment instead of taking one from the
caller, so the callers don't need to keep it alive.

This is a preparation for installing launchers through the XDG
DynamicLauncher portal, which is an asynchronous D-Bus API. Every
operation still completes synchronously.

Also fixes DeleteAllDesktopShortcuts() skipping the remaining deletions
after the first failure, due to short-circuit evaluation.

[Android] Reject URIs whose authority differs from their string form

Callers of ContentUriUtils.resolveContentUriOwner() check a Uri object
but may then use only its string form, e.g. passing it to native, which
later passes it back to Java to be reparsed with Uri.parse() and opened.
A Uri object can disagree with its string form: on Android Q, a
HierarchicalUri unparcelled from another app can carry independent
encoded and decoded authorities, and an OpaqueUri reports a null
authority even when its string form includes one. Neither is produced
by Uri.parse() or by apps behaving normally.

resolveContentUriOwner() now compares the object's authority with the
authority of its reparsed string form, and if they differ (including an
OpaqueUri with an authority in its string form), returns
NON_EXPORTED_FROM_CURRENT_APP, the most restrictive owner, so that all
callers reject it. Previously an OpaqueUri was resolved through its
string form, so an opaque URI naming another app's provider was
reported as OTHER_APP.

[LHS] Keep hybrid rail folded on NTP_LHS_READY

Previously, NTP_LHS_READY unconditionally set isExpanded_ = true,
causing the preloaded expanded LHS iframe to auto-open on NTP load even
in hybrid mode. Remove isExpanded_ = true from the NTP_LHS_READY handler
so hybrid mode starts folded until user interaction while non-hybrid
mode continues showing #expanded once ready.

Serialize CSSUnparsedValue directly in toString

CSSUnparsedValue previously relied on the base CSSStyleValue::toString()
implementation, which converted the object into a CSSValue via
ToCSSValue() and validated declaration-value syntax. When invoked off the
main thread, this entered CSS parser code paths that depend on
main-thread-only data structures.

This change overrides CSSUnparsedValue::toString() to serialize segments
and tokens directly per specification, avoiding unnecessary CSS value
conversion and parsing during stringification. In addition, explicit
thread affinity checks are added to ToCSSValue() and
ConsumeUnparsedDeclaration() to ensure declaration parsing remains on
the main thread.

Fix corruption due to reentrancy in NodeRareData

NodeRareData::EnsureDisplayLockContext constructs a new
DisplayLockContext *after* it has already taken a pointer to its
destination slot in dynamic NodeRareData memory. The DisplayLockContext
constructor can itself trigger an addition to NodeRareData, and if the
reentrant addition causes a reallocation of NodeRareData storage, then
the outer invocation will be left holding an invalid pointer.

This CL switches EnsureDisplayLockContext to construct the new instance
before calling into NodeRareData.

[Unified Tabstrip] Repaint tab containers on declutter separator change

Schedule a repaint on both the pinned and unpinned tab containers in
TabStripView::UpdateSeparatorVisibility (via OnChildCountChanged) when
adding or removing tabs crosses
TabStyle::kTabStripDeclutterMinTabsForSeparatorHide in horizontal
orientation with kTabStripDeclutter enabled.

In the unified horizontal tab strip, PinnedTabContainerView and
UnpinnedTabContainerView live in separate layer-backed ScrollViews.
Because pinned tabs keep fixed bounds when unpinned tabs are added or
removed (and unpinned tabs can also keep fixed bounds at standard or
minimum width), crossing the 20-tab declutter separator threshold
previously left pinned tab separators stale until hovering a pinned tab
triggered a repaint.

Fixed: 559189588
Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=*HorizontalSeparators*

SpdySessionPool: Don't save alt-service information with invalid cert.

When the user allows an invalid cert for an H2 connection, and the
connection tries to provide alt-service information, ignore the alt
service information. This matches behavior elsewhere (e.g., in
HttpNetworkTransaction::ProcessAltSvcHeader()).

The reason for this is that this information is persisted, so a single
server allowed to use a bad cert once, could create an alt service
entry that would persist for years. While alt-service entries do not
bypass cert validity checks, we'd still try to talk to the alt service
location every time a user connects to a server, which would not be
great.
